sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Novi, Michigan?
sections.html:
The City of Novi Treasurer's Office bills and collects the tax on Novi homes, and the city's Assessing Department sets the values the bill is built from. The treasurer works from 45175 Ten Mile Road, Novi, MI 48375, and answers tax questions at 248-347-0440. The Treasurer page also links the online property and tax search.

Novi sits in Oakland County, about 25 miles northwest of downtown Detroit, and covers roughly 30 square miles of land around Walled Lake. I-96, I-696, I-275 and M-5 all reach the city, and the population rose from about 9,700 in 1970 to 66,243 in 2020. Novi became a city in 1969, after starting life as a township in 1832.

The city is only the collecting agent for most of what appears on the statement. Its own operating taxes are billed in full on the summer statement, while the winter statement carries the county, school and authority levies. Novi has no say over the county and school rates.

sections.h2: When are Novi property taxes due?
sections.html:
Novi's summer bill is due by the end of August and the winter bill by mid February. The city's 2026 notice said summer bills would be mailed the week of July 1 and that payments had to reach the treasurer on or before August 31 to avoid an automatic penalty. That date has passed for 2026, so the next one to watch is the winter deadline.

Novi billing calendar, from the city's 2026 summer notice and its winter statement

A drop box sits behind the Civic Center, and the 2026 notice accepted drop box payments until midnight on the deadline day. Online payment by credit card or electronic check is available through cityofnovi.org. Be careful with the bank numbers you type, because a returned payment after the due date draws the penalty.

sections.h2: How is the taxable value of a Novi home set?
sections.html:
Novi taxes a house on its taxable value, which is usually lower than half of what the home would sell for. The assessor estimates market value as of Tax Day, December 31 of the year before, and the assessed value is about 50% of that. For 2026 the city used a 24-month sales study running from April 1, 2023 to March 31, 2025, covering roughly 2,000 sales.

Taxable value grows more slowly than assessed value. The 2026 inflation rate multiplier is 1.027, so a home that stays with its owner can rise no more than 2.7%, even if neighborhood prices climbed 10%. The city's formula is the prior taxable value, less losses, times the multiplier, plus additions.

  • Taxable value is the lesser of assessed value and capped value.
  • The tax equals taxable value divided by 1,000, times the millage rate.
  • A sale resets the taxable value to the assessed value the following year.
  • Special assessments, trash charges and penalties are added on top.

The reset after a sale matters to a seller because the next owner's bill will likely be larger than yours. A buyer who compares your old bill with what they will owe can be misled, so point them to the assessed value instead.

sections.h2: How can a Novi owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
A Novi owner appeals at the March Board of Review, and that is the only time a current assessment can be challenged. The board opens the second Monday in March, and the Notice of Assessment is mailed in mid February. Petition forms come from the Assessing Department or the city's website, and you make an appointment to appear.

If the board's answer is not acceptable, the next level is the Michigan Tax Tribunal. A residential petition must go to the Tribunal at 611 W. Ottawa St., Lansing, MI 48933 by July 31, and only after you have appeared before the March board. Commercial and industrial appeals to the Tribunal are due May 31. The July and December boards cannot hear value disputes under MCL 211.53b.

Two relief options sit outside the appeal process. Michigan has no age-based property tax break, but Novi offers an annual poverty exemption based on income and assets, which needs Board of Review approval. Owners who qualify can also ask the Treasurer's Office about deferring summer taxes.

sections.h2: Where does a Novi tax bill go?
sections.html:
On the city's sample winter statement, about 59% of a homestead bill went to education, 30% to the City of Novi and 11% to Oakland County. That split was based on the Novi and OCC district homestead rates, so a parcel in another district will differ. Several school systems reach into the city.

  • Novi Community Schools cover most of the city.
  • Northville Public Schools serve a large part of the south side.
  • Walled Lake Consolidated Schools take in a pocket with two elementary schools.
  • South Lyon Community Schools hold a small western strip.

The statement's other lines include the county parks and recreation levy, the zoo authority, the art institute, Oakland transit and the Huron Clinton Metropolitan Authority. Check the parcel number and school district code on your own bill before you compare it with a neighbor's.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Novi homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page counts 67,319 Novi residents in July 2025 and 26,801 households for 2020 to 2024. Owners occupy 66.3% of housing units, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $421,900. Median gross rent is $1,747, and median household income is $110,723.

Those figures describe the whole city, so a condo near the I-96 corridor and a lakeside house will sit well apart. Roughly 29% of residents were born abroad, and the city's economy leans on health care, automotive suppliers and retail around Novi Road and I-96.

sections.h2: What happens if Novi property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid Novi tax is returned to the county after the winter period ends. Under MCL 211.78a, taxes still owing on March 1 are returned as delinquent, and a 4% county fee and interest of 1% per month are added. The Oakland County Treasurer then collects, and continued nonpayment leads into a three-year foreclosure process.

The county's current notice for 2024 and earlier balances names March 31, 2027 as the last day to pay and keep the property. The treasurer's office can set up repayment schedules and refers owners to other programs; its line is 248-858-0611. Our Oakland County property tax guide walks through the foreclosure steps in order.

sections.h2: How does the principal residence exemption affect a Novi sale?
sections.html:
The principal residence exemption removes up to 18 mills of school operating tax from a home you own and live in. You must own and occupy the house on or before June 1 to see the reduction on the summer bill, and a winter exemption exists for homes acquired between June 2 and November 1.

When you sell, file the Request to Rescind form with the Assessing Department so the exemption ends on the right date. If you have already bought a new Michigan home, a conditional rescission can keep the exemption on the old one while it is actively listed, provided it is empty, unleased and not used for business. The form and a copy of the new exemption must reach the city by June 1 for both bills, or by November 1 for the winter bill.

sections.h2: How is tax handled when you sell a house in Novi?
sections.html:
The title company prorates the current year's tax between you and the buyer and pays anything past due from your proceeds. Ask the city treasurer for the current balance, and ask the county for an official delinquent tax statement if any year has gone to Oakland County. Oakland's Property Gateway sells those statements to owners and title companies.

A sale with tax owing can still close, because the payoff comes out of the seller's side of the settlement statement. What costs sellers money is surprise: a missed winter deadline adds a 3% penalty that nobody at the counter can waive. Settle the unpaid amount early, and keep copies of both statements for the year of sale.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Novi winter taxes without a penalty?
faqs.a: February 14. The city's winter statement lists payment from December 1 through February 14, and the money must be physically received by then. A 3% penalty applies from the next day, and the treasurer cannot waive it.

faqs.q: Does Novi accept postmarks as proof of on-time payment?
faqs.a: No. The city's notices say postmarks and post-dated checks are not accepted. Use the drop box behind the Civic Center, pay online, or mail early enough to arrive before the deadline.

faqs.q: Will my Novi taxes jump after I buy a house?
faqs.a: Often yes. The year after a sale, taxable value resets to the assessed value, which can be well above the prior owner's capped figure. After that, increases are limited to the inflation multiplier or 5%, whichever is less.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Novi assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Novi Assessing Department, which handles values, exemptions and name or address changes. Tax bills and payments go to the Treasurer's Office at 248-347-0440.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Novi house if the taxes are behind?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the unpaid balance, with any penalty and interest, from your proceeds at closing. Get a current statement from the city or, for earlier years, from the Oakland County Treasurer first.
